...Respondents
(By Sri. D.L. Ransa Vasanthi, Hcgp For R1;
 Sri. K. Vasanth, Advocate For R2 & R3)
 This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226
And 227 Of The Constitution Of India Praying To
i) Issue A Writ In The Nature Of Certiorari Quashing
The General Awards Dated:22.03.2021 Bearing No.
Kiadb/Laq:1988.2020-21 Vide Annexure-A Passed By The
3Rd Respondent And Etc.
 This Petition, Coming On For Preliminary
Hearing, This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The present petition is filed by the petitioner seeking for a writ of certiorari to quash the general award passed by respondent No.3-KIADB on 22.03.2021 in respect of NC: 2023:KHC:33309 property bearing Survey No.112/3, measuring 20 guntas situated at Mindahalli Village, Kasaba Hobli, Malur Taluk, Kolar District and for a further direction to the respondents to consider the case of the petitioner as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, 1966.

2. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that though as on the date the general Smt Krishnamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66209665/
2 award was passed there was neither any litigation pending nor was there any impediment for the respondents to pass the consent award as per Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act, 1966, the Respondent No.3 proceeded to pass the general award and that in view of the law laid down in Smt. Rathnamma vs. The State of Karnataka in W.P.No.31702/2018 dated 29.11.2018 passing of the consent award under Section 29(2) is not only beneficial but would also put an end to the challenge to the award.

sentences.text: Hence, he submits that the general award in the circumstances be set aside and the respondents be directed to pass the consent award.

In response, Sri.Vasanth K, learned counsel for respondents -KIADB submits that the issue involved in the present petition is covered by the order dated 29.11.2018 passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.31702/2018.
He further submits the present petition may also be disposed of, subject to the directions issued in the said order.

4. Heard and perused the records.
5.
Under the identical circumstances, this Court in its order dated 29.11.2018 passed in W.P.31702/2018 while allowing the writ petition, has issued following directions:

"4. In view of the above, this writ petition succeeds in terms of the decision cited above; a Writ of Certiorari issues quashing the impugned award dated 13.4.2017 at Annexure-E so far as it relates to the lands of the petitioner only for the purpose of determination and payment of the compensation as if the award is by agreement under Section 29 (2) of the Act, leaving the vested title to the land in the respondent-KIADB, otherwise unaffected".
NC: 2023:KHC:33309 6.
In that view of the matter, petitioner is also entitled to the benefit of similar order.

Hence, the following:
ORDER 1. The writ petition is allowed.
2.
The general award dated 22.03.2021 as per Annexure-A insofar as it relates to the extent of the petitioner's land is hereby set aside.

3. The respondents are directed to consider the case of the petitioner in terms of the order/directions extracted herein above within a period of three months from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
